title: SLO onboarding pocket guide & weekly sprint notes
content:
Purpose:
A compact, action-first guide for partners (product, serving-runtime, SRE, support) to onboard a new service to the company SLO fabric. Combines a one-page checklist with the running sprint notes for the first 6 weeks. Meant to be carried in your backlog, paired with PLAT-842 (template work) and the confluence onboarding doc.

Audience:
- Platform engineers and SRE liaisons
- Product managers and feature owners shipping model-serving endpoints
- Solutions & support oncall handoff contacts

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- Service has a measurable, agreed SLO and attached error budget policy before public launch.
- Observability signals (latency p50/p95, error-rate, queue-depth) are wired to the SLO dashboard within 2 sprints.
- Runbook with clear escalation chain created and linked to incident playbooks.
- Canary + rollback policy validated end-to-end in staging.

One-page onboarding checklist (use as a ticket template):
1) Define customer-facing SLA/SLO pair: owner, metric, threshold, and review cadence.
   - Owner: <name/email>
   - Metric: e.g., request success rate (200 OK), or inference-complete within 300ms p95
   - Threshold: e.g., 99.5% success over 7d window
   - Review: weekly for first 6 weeks, then monthly
2) Instrumentation smoke test:
   - Ensure request traces include model id, route, and latency buckets
   - Expose derived SLO metric in metrics store (prometheus/grafana or datadog)
   - Add a synthetic heartbeat that exercises the model path every 5m
3) Alerting & paging:
   - Create alerts for SLO burn-rate > 2x and for latency spikes (p95 > threshold)
   - Define paging rota and escalation matrix in the runbook
4) Canary/rollout plan:
   - Canary duration: min 1h or 5000 requests, whichever comes first
   - Success criteria: no more than 0.5% error-rate increase vs baseline
   - Fallback: automatic traffic cutover to stable variant / lower-capacity tier
5) Failure-mode runbook & recovery script links:
   - Cache warmup script, KV reset, model-variant swap procedure
   - Post-incident: ticket template for RCA and customer-impact mapping
6) Cost guardrails & autoscaling knobs:
   - Set soft limits on batch sizes and GPU concurrency for canary
   - Attach cost-to-serve estimate to the rollout ticket
7) Data & compliance check (if private/dedicated):
   - Confirm KMS keys and audit logging are enabled
   - Verify network policy (VPC/NAT) for private deployments

Quick reference: Recommended SLO metric choices by product type:
- Low-latency API (chat/compose): latency p95 and percent-success (200 OK).
- Batch embeddings: throughput and per-batch failure-rate.
- Long-running reranking jobs: completion rate within SLA window.

Who signs off when:
- Product owner: SLO definition and customer impact statement
- Platform SRE: instrumentation + alerts configured
- Serving runtime lead: canary and fallback validated
- Security/compliance: signoff for private deployments

Week-by-week sprint notes (working log, remove when finalized):
Week 0 (prep) — 2026-02-10
- Kickoff call notes: agreed metric: inference-success-rate (binary), latency p95 target 350ms
- Action: PLAT-842 created to generate dashboard + alert template (owner: Ethan)
- Question: Does product want user-visible SLA or internal SLO? (TODO owner: María)

Week 1 — 2026-02-16
- Instrumentation: traces instrumented, metrics pipeline end-to-end to staging grafana.
- Synthetic job stub added; observed baseline p95=290ms on staging GPU pool.
- Open risks: synthetic load is lower than expected production concurrency — need load generator (Samir)

Week 2 — 2026-02-23
- Canary harness built; default canary traffic route implemented in routing service.
- Alert thresholds drafted: burn-rate alert, latency-slide rule.
- Action items:
  - Samir to provision load-generator VM and run 30m spike test by 2/25
  - Lena to draft runbook escalation steps and include non-blocking contact list

Week 3 — 2026-03-01
- Spike test results: under 2x production concurrency, p95 jumped to 420ms when batch-size auto-scaling not engaged.
- Immediate mitigation: reduce default batch size to 16 for canary; retest.
- Decision: postpone public rollout until batch autoscaler tuned (owner: serving-runtime)
- Notes: draft RCA template added to linked_artifacts: JIRA:PLAT-842

Open issues and questions (to triage in weekly reliability sync):
- Capacity tagging: do we have a clear allocation for dedicated pools vs shared-hosted? (affects routing fallback)
- Cost annex: who owns the per-feature cost projection for committed capacity? (product or platform?)
- Runbook discoverability: ensure runbook is linked from the service's repo README and from the SLO dashboard

Risk register (short):
- Risk: Inaccurate synthetic load -> false sense of safety. Mitigation: sample production traffic via replay for 48h window in staging. Owner: Samir
- Risk: Alerts noisy during rollout. Mitigation: use burn-rate multisignal alerting and mute during canary window. Owner: Ethan
- Risk: Missing compliance checks for private customers. Mitigation: pre-launch compliance checklist and signoff gate. Owner: María

Hand-off checklist for SRE on-call (before M1 public traffic):
- Verify synthetic heartbeat has run successfully for 72h without SLO violations
- Ensure the alerting rota is populated for next 30 days
- Confirm canary rollback automation exists and is tested
- Validate cost center tags and telemetry lineage

Notes to self / quick wins (informal):
- Keep the onboarding ticket intentionally small — aim for an MVP SLO first, iterate on secondary metrics later
- Embed a small script in the template that populates a dashboard with example thresholds to reduce friction

Next steps (immediate):
- Samir: production traffic replay plan + VM (due 2026-03-05)
- Ethan: finalize alert suppression policy for canary windows (due 2026-03-04)
- María: confirm compliance signoff owners (due 2026-03-03)

If you copy this doc to a service folder, rename to service-slo-onboard-pocket.json and update the owner field.

Unresolved questions to bring to the cross-functional sync:
- Should SLO burn-rate thresholds be standardized across all low-latency APIs, or negotiated per service?
- How aggressive should automatic fallback be for Dedicated customers to avoid SLA violations?

End of doc.
